This posting is for an existing vacancy.



Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. 

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone https://blog.1password.com/inside-the-culture-powering-1passwords-next-chapter/. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. 

How we work with AI
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.

To us, this means we do ask that you join live interviews without using AI tools so we can get to know how you communicate, solve problems, and collaborate with others.

Our approach to remote work 
We believe in the power of remote work, but recognize that in-person connection is important to help us achieve our mission. While we are a remote-first company, travel for in-person engagement is a part of almost all roles, and we require our employees to be ready and willing to take part. Media buying is now the easy part. 
 In 2026, the buying itself is piping. The levers that actually move a DTC account are creative, offer, and conversion rate, and the platform keeps getting better at rewarding whoever gets those right.
 So we don't hire media buyers. We hire marketers who buy media.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands across our service lines, 20 to 25 of them on paid media, and we spend $6-9M a month on Meta. We're hiring one person to own a handful of those accounts end to end.
 Here's what "end to end" actually means here.
 You are the account manager. We don't have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership and accountability: when you're the person answering for the account, it's your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You are the creative strategist. You do the research, you find the angles, and you write the briefs and the scripts. You direct our editors and designers rather than filing requests with them. Creative isn't a ticket you submit. It's your job.
 You build the things the account needs. If conversion rate is the bottleneck, you build the landing page. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You carry up to six accounts. That's the capacity we run at today, and the team averages about four and a half. You'll manage far fewer accounts than you would at most agencies. In exchange you get real ownership of the results and you get to work as an end to end marketer instead of one station on an assembly line.
 You can live anywhere. We're a remote team and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you're the client's point of contact and there's nobody else to cover it. The rest of your day is yours.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we'll both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 We're growing fast and we keep the bar high. 
 We believe the best media buyer today is a sharp marketer who uses AI every day. We built an internal creative analysis tool that connects to Claude, and we use Pipeboard to read and write to ad accounts and run heavy analysis. You don't need to know our stack yet. You do need to actually use AI in your work, not be afraid of it, and teach yourself what you don't know.
 What the job looks like
 Own 4 to 6 DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, the creative lead, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $30k/mo to $1M/mo.
 Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you're the one who answers when something isn't working.
 Run the research before the ads. Marketing is 80% research here. You mine customer reviews, ad comments, support tickets, and Reddit for the language and objections that become angles. You pull competitor ad libraries. You run our internal tooling that OCRs and transcribes the ads in your account and ties them to performance, so you know what winning and losing actually look like in this account.
 Write the briefs and the scripts, and direct the work. Creative direction is yours. You run revision rounds with our editors and designers and you hold the quality bar.
 Ship creative on a cadence. Roughly 8 to 10 new ad launches a week is where accounts hold, in batches every 1 to 1.5 weeks. Informed volume, not spray and pray. We want better hypotheses, not more randomness.
 Build and test landing pages. Advertorials, comparison pages, PDPs. Built in Claude Code, deployed to Vercel, tested live on a subdomain before anything gets pushed into the client's theme.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Report on new customer economics. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended ROAS and not last click. You'll be expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.
 You're a fit if
 You've done this with real money. Hands-on Meta at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them.
 You're AI-native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude (or equivalent) as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it. If you can research, write, and build a converting page from scratch, we can teach you the buying.
 You can write direct response in English at a native or near-native level. Hooks, scripts, ad copy, advertorial. In the customer's own words, not invented. This is the single biggest source of leverage in the role and the thing we screen hardest for. If writing persuasive English isn't a strength, this isn't the job.
 You can communicate your ideas. This matters as much as anything else on this list. You'll be in front of clients constantly with nobody in between, so you need to be able to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire.
 You have taste and you know when to hand off. You direct creative, you don't half-build it yourself. AI slop shipped to a client is a habit we break, not a shortcut we accept.
 You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
 Bonus: you've built or operated your own Shopify store or eComm brand. Several of our team have, and it shows.
 You're not a fit if
 "That wasn't my role" is in your vocabulary. It's the fastest way to end an interview here. If creative was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the creative.
 You want to be told what to do this week.
 You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
 Why This Role Is Exciting
 This is not a maintenance job. You will be surrounded by people who move fast, care a lot, and take the work seriously.
 You will work on real brands with real budgets.  We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
 You will grow into senior strategy.  We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

 SUMMARY OF DUTIES 
 Reporting to a Supervisor, Hamilton Paramedic Service, the paramedic provides primary emergency medical care and transportation for ill and/or injured persons in the community to, from, and between treatment facilities, in specially equipped ambulance vehicles and emergency response vehicles. Paramedics also contribute to non-emergency and multi-disciplinary approaches to community care, through avenues such as public education, harm reduction, community paramedicine, palliative care, and other related programming. 
 GENERAL DUTIES 
 Provide primary emergency medical care for ill and/or injured persons at the emergency site by providing basic and advanced pre-hospital life support. 
 Provide transportation for ill and/or injured persons, to, from, and between treatment facilities, in specially equipped ambulance vehicles as directed by the Central Ambulance Communications Centre (CACC). 
 Deliver thorough patient assessment and treatment in accordance with Provincial and local standards and medical directives. 
 Responsible for all medical interventions as deemed essential by the Base Hospital and Hamilton Paramedic Service including controlled drug therapy, manual defibrillation and cardiac dysrhythmia interpretation according to Provincial Medical Directives.  
 Interact with members of the health care team, allied emergency care providers, the public, and patients in a professional manner. 
 Maintain communication with and follow the directions of all Central Ambulance Communication Centres (CACCs) encountered during operations, ensuring each CACC is kept informed of the paramedic’s status and location. 
 Assume a role of leadership, as required, and uphold patient advocacy. 
 Collaborate with medical personnel and allied emergency care providers to facilitate prompt treatment, support, and advocacy for the patients, their family and friends during the time of emergency care. 
 Participate in primary care, public health, public education, and community events as assigned. 
 Check, maintain, and stock fleet vehicles so-as to maintain the vehicle and vehicle equipment in a clean/sanitary, mechanically safe state of readiness in accordance with local and provincial standards.  Report any vehicle and/or equipment deficiencies and assist in corrective action where qualified. 
 Inspect, restock, and maintain ambulance stations in a clean and operational state. 
 Prepare various reports as required.  This includes, but is not limited to: Ambulance Call Reports, Incident/Occurrence Reports, Logistics Reports, Vehicle Inspection Reports, and any other report as deemed necessary by the Hamilton Paramedic Service and/or the Ministry of Health and Long-Term Care.  
 Participate in Continuing Education as required and participate in the training/precepting of Advanced Care and Primary Care paramedic students and other allied healthcare professionals. 
 Maintain all legislated requirements for employment and all certification requirements as set by the Base Hospital, the Hamilton Paramedic Service, and the MOHLTC. 
 Perform other duties as assigned which are directly related to the major responsibilities of the job. 
 QUALIFICATIONS 
 1. Must be a current and active certified Primary Care Paramedic, Advanced Care Paramedic, or Critical Care Paramedic with at least 1.5 years (18 months) of full-time (or equivalent hours) experience operating in a 911 capacity. 
 2. Diploma from an approved Ontario Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) College Training Program. 
 3. If graduation was prior to 2003, candidates must provide proof of completion of all mandatory Ministry of Health and Long-Term Care core programs via individual certificates or with a letter attesting to completion by an approved Ontario PCP Training Program. 
 4. Current Basic Life Support (BLS) Provider certificate or CPR HCP certificate or advanced cardiac life support (ACLS) certificate. 
 5. Hold the qualification of, or have obtained a pass standing, in an advanced emergency medical care assistant examination (A-EMCA), or equivalent, as outlined in the Ambulance Act O. Reg. 257/00. 
 6. Must hold and maintain a valid Ontario Driver's Licence that authorizes the person to drive an ambulance. 
 7. Must meet all current requirements (including medical) of the Ambulance Act and Regulations, including the current Ambulance Service Communicable Disease Standards.  As a condition of employment, you will be required to provide proof of the minimum requirements required as outlined in the Ambulance Act and Regulations. 
 8. Must successfully complete any/all requirements and become fully certified by the Centre for Paramedic Education and Research (CPER) with Hamilton Health Sciences (HHS) Base Hospital Program. 
 9. Demonstrated ability to read, write and speak English proficiently. 
 10. Proven ability to demonstrated leadership and take command during emergency situations. 
 11. Must be in good physical health and capable of lifting heavy weights. 
 12. Proven ability to exercise sound judgement in emergency situations.

About Moment Energy 
 Independent energy is here. Help us deploy it. 
 Energy should be free. Free from aging grids, fragile supply chains, and unnecessary extraction. At Moment Energy, we’re building a world where clean power is abundant, affordable, and uninterrupted for everyone. 
 The world doesn’t need another promise about energy; it needs proof that a freer future is possible. Moment Energy is the pragmatic liberator of power, the only company certified to turn the largest untapped energy supply into independent energy. 
 Now is the moment. While the industry scraps millions of batteries with decades of life left, we put them to work by repurposing large-format batteries into advanced battery energy storage systems that deliver real-world impact. 
 We were told second-life batteries would never be safe enough or scalable enough. We didn’t argue, we engineered the solution. Today, Moment Energy delivers 5x the energy density and holds the certifications required to deploy energy independence at scale. 
 Now is the moment. Join us. 
 The Opportunity 
 We are seeking a detail-oriented and hands-on Electrical Test Engineer to join our dynamic team. This role is crucial for ensuring the safety, reliability, and performance of our innovative battery energy storage systems (BESS). You will spend the majority of your time (80%+) in the R&D and production lab, setting up, running, and analyzing a wide variety of tests. You will also be expected to develop Testers from the ground up, and support the broader test team with custom PCBs that will help simplify our Testers and reduce cost. Your work will directly contribute to our product development, certification, and overall success. If you are passionate about clean technology and thrive in a hands-on, fast-paced environment, this is the role for you.
 Responsibilities and Duties 
 Develop, execute, and document comprehensive test plans for various needs, including certification, compliance, R&D, component validation, and lifecycle testing.
 Take primary ownership of hands-on test setup, including the wiring of thermocouples, power supplies, fuses, contactors, cameras, and cooling bench setups.
 Design and build custom R&D test setups to prototype novel concepts and investigate failure modes.
 Design PCBs and power electronics for in-house testers, with the goal of making them more capable, easier to operate, and cheaper to build. 
 Build certification test setups from cell up to BESS-level for pre-compliance tests and live witness testing by certified test labs. 
 Work directly with high-voltage DC and AC systems (up to 1000VDC, 600VAC), ensuring all safety protocols are rigorously followed.
 Operate and manage battery cyclers to perform tests on cells, modules, racks, and full BESS units.
 Set up and configure data acquisition systems (Agilent DAQ, NI) for data capture of various signals (CAN, ModBus, temperature, humidity, voltage, current, etc.)
 Utilize standard test equipment such as oscilloscopes, power supplies, and multimeters to diagnose and validate system performance.
 Create and develop scripts to automate test equipment, data gathering, and long-term tests.
 Analyze test data using Python, summarize findings, and create clear, concise reports and presentations for the engineering team.
 Support the team with abuse testing, including sample preparation and test setup coordination.
 Maintain, troubleshoot, and calibrate lab test equipment to ensure accuracy and reliability.
 Contribute to the creation of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for testing and lab activities.
 The Candidate 
 We’re looking for individuals with the following traits, skills, and experiences: 
 Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related technical field.
 2+ years of experience in a hands-on testing, validation, or verification role.
 Demonstrated experience working safely with high-voltage DC and AC systems.
 PCB design experience (schematic capture and layout in Altium, KiCad, or similar), especially for test fixtures or low-volume hardware, with examples of past projects.
 Proven ability to create test plans, design experiments, and document results.
 Hands-on proficiency in wiring, soldering, and assembling complex electro-mechanical test setups.
 Experience with data acquisition hardware and software (DAQ systems, Python, etc.).
 Familiarity with industrial communication protocols such as CAN or Modbus.
 Why join us? 
 Today, we’re delivering 5x the energy density and have all the certifications needed to ship energy independence to the world. 
 Be part of a mission-driven company focused on creating sustainable energy solutions and making a positive impact on the world. 
 Collaborate closely with passionate co-founders and a team committed to innovation and excellence. 
 Contribute to building and scaling a company from the ground up, where your work will have a direct and meaningful impact. 
 Thrive in a workplace that values collaboration, wellness, and celebrating successes, with regular company socials, fitness sessions, and more. 
 We're a fast-paced and dynamic team. 
 Every day you'll be taking on a new challenge and learning something new. You'll take on a wide breadth of tasks and contribute to disrupting the battery industry. You'll be part of a tight-knit team that is working together to save the planet! Fun, health, and wellness are incorporated into our daily schedule and we encourage all our team members to bring innovative ideas to the table to create an interactive workplace. 
 Moment Energy Benefits Highlights (full time, permanent employees only) 
 Financial Growth: Employee equity and a robust RRSP matching program. 
 Comprehensive Health Coverage: Extended health, dental, and vision benefits for you and your dependents through Manulife.
 Generous Time Off & Flexibility: Paid time off plus a paid company closure between Christmas and New Year's, with a generous paid sick leave.
 Vibrant Culture & Perks: Open and collaborative office culture, frequent company socials and wellness programs (weekly yoga/fitness), and free EV charging on-site.
 Company Dinner: Weekly Tuesday dinner provided by Moment Energy. We also have a generous supply of coffee and snacks for the office! 
 Our Commitments 
 Moment Energy is an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to inclusive, barrier-free recruitment and selection processes, including our work environment. We especially welcome applications from Indigenous peoples, members of racialized communities, persons with disabilities, women, and persons who identify as 2SLGBTQ+. 
 —--- 
 Our Values 
 Our values are key to how we show up every day at Moment Energy! We keep them in the forefront of what we do, and they’re used everywhere. We refer to them when we have tough decisions to make, we give shoutouts based on living out these values, and we include them as part of our performance reviews. 
 We have 5 core values and 1 foundational pillar (Safety is our Foundation) which lays the groundwork for everything we do. 
 Safety is our Foundation 
 We prioritize the safety of our products, customers, employees, and the general public above all else. Tenstorrent is leading the industry on cutting-edge AI technology, revolutionizing performance expectations, ease of use, and cost efficiency. With AI redefining the computing paradigm, solutions must evolve to unify innovations in software models, compilers, platforms, networking, and semiconductors. Our diverse team of technologists have developed a high performance RISC-V CPU from scratch, and share a passion for AI and a deep desire to build the best AI platform possible. We value collaboration, curiosity, and a commitment to solving hard problems. We are growing our team and looking for contributors of all seniorities.
 Tenstorrent is looking for a Workload Performance Optimization Engineer to help optimize the software workloads that run on our next-generation RISC-V platforms. You’ll work across modern datacenter and agentic AI workloads—including Java, Python, PHP, Node.js, Lua, Go, and Rust—to identify performance bottlenecks and develop software, compiler, runtime, and hardware-aware optimizations that improve throughput, latency, and efficiency. This role sits at the intersection of software runtimes, compilers, CPU microarchitecture, and RISC-V silicon. You’ll bring up and tune major runtimes, profile real-world applications, investigate memory and concurrency behavior, and explore optimizations using RISC-V Vector/Matrix capabilities and custom instructions. You’ll also work with AI-assisted development and automated optimization workflows to accelerate the performance engineering process. Your work will directly influence both the RISC-V software ecosystem and the architecture of future Tenstorrent CPUs.
 This role is remote, based out of North America.
 We welcome candidates at various experience levels for this role. During the interview process, candidates will be assessed for the appropriate level, and offers will align with that level, which may differ from the one in this posting.
 Who You Are 
 You’re a performance engineer who enjoys getting deep into runtimes, compilers, applications, and CPU microarchitecture to understand why software is fast—or slow.
 You have hands-on experience optimizing software on RISC-V or another modern CPU architecture, with a strong understanding of the hardware/software boundary.
 You’re comfortable profiling complex systems, finding bottlenecks, forming hypotheses, and iterating through optimizations using data.
 You’re excited about emerging agentic AI development workflows and using AI tools to automate profiling, coding, benchmarking, and optimization.
 You’re a strong technical collaborator who can work across compiler, runtime, systems software, hardware, and performance modeling teams.
 What We Need 
 Master’s or PhD in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, with strong experience in performance optimization, computer architecture, compilers, or systems software.
 Hands-on experience with runtime or compiler optimization, such as OpenJDK/JIT, LLVM, GCC, V8, Python, or equivalent systems.
 Strong understanding of CPU performance, memory hierarchies, concurrency, garbage collection, vector/SIMD optimization, and RISC-V architecture.
 Expertise with performance profiling and analysis tools such as Linux perf, runtime profilers, QEMU, tracing tools, and performance modeling environments.
 Strong programming skills in Java, Python, C/C++, and RISC-V assembly, with the ability to work effectively across multiple software layers.
 What You Will Learn 
 How to optimize modern software stacks from application and runtime all the way down to CPU microarchitecture and silicon.
 How RISC-V Vector, Matrix, and custom ISA capabilities can be used to accelerate real-world datacenter and AI workloads.
 How runtime, compiler, memory, and concurrency decisions impact performance at datacenter scale.
 How to build automated and AI-assisted performance optimization workflows that continuously profile, analyze, modify, and benchmark software.
 How to influence future CPU architecture by connecting real workload behavior and software optimization opportunities to hardware design decisions.

Job Description Summary 
Vous aspirez à concrétiser des projets d’infrastructure d’envergure tout en plaçant la santé, la sécurité et l’excellence opérationnelle au cœur de vos priorités ? Si vous souhaitez faire une réelle différence dans votre région et participer activement à la nouvelle ère énergétique, rejoignez-nous.
Chez GE Vernova, vous jouez un rôle stratégique pour bâtir un monde qui fonctionne, en guidant nos équipes vers la réussite sur les chantiers au Québec.
Vous aurez l'occasion d'évoluer aux côtés des meilleurs talents de l'industrie, de travailler sur des technologies de pointe et de faire partie d’une équipe mondiale d’environ 75 000 personnes réparties dans plus de 100 pays.
Votre rôle: 
Vous prendrez la direction de plusieurs chantiers hydroélectriques d’envergure au Québec, menés de front en simultané.
Votre mandat: 
Mobiliser les équipes sur le terrain, garantir une exécution sécuritaire et performante, et piloter chaque projet de la planification initiale jusqu’à la mise en service.
Évoluant au sein d’une structure matricielle, vous collaborerez étroitement avec les chargés de projets ainsi que les équipes d’ingénierie et d’approvisionnement. Votre aptitude à tisser des liens de confiance et à exercer un leadership d’influence sera déterminante pour harmoniser les priorités des différents partenaires et répondre aux réalités du terrain. 
 Job Description 
 Ce que vous ferez 
 Protéger la santé et la sécurité de nos équipes, veiller à la qualité irréprochable des travaux et assurer le respect rigoureux des exigences environnementales et réglementaires. 
 Piloter les activités de plusieurs chantiers en simultané tout en encadrant et soutenant les équipes de gestion, de supervision et de construction. 
 Traduire les objectifs stratégiques des projets en plans d'exécution opérationnels, en coordonnant efficacement la main-d’œuvre, les équipements, les matériaux et les sous-traitants. 
 Optimiser la gestion des échéanciers, des coûts, des risques et des engagements contractuels en mobilisant les bonnes compétences pour résoudre rapidement les enjeux. 
 Harmoniser les relations entre les corps de métier et les fonctions partenaires pour aligner les besoins du terrain sur les priorités globales des projets. 
 Cultiver des partenariats durables avec les clients et les sous-traitants, tout en participant activement à la mobilisation de la main-d’œuvre locale au Québec. 
 Ce que nous recherchons 
 Le profil recherché se distingue par une solide expertise en direction de chantiers complexes, un leadership mobilisateur et une capacité avérée à mener à terme des projets majeurs en milieu industriel ou d'infrastructure. 
 Requis : 
 Formation : Un diplôme en génie, en construction ou dans un domaine connexe, ou une expérience professionnelle équivalente reconnue. 
 Expérience : Plus de 10 ans d’expérience en direction de chantiers ou de projets d’envergure, idéalement dans les secteurs de l’hydroélectricité, de l’énergie ou des infrastructures lourdes, incluant la gestion multi-chantiers en parallèle. 
 Connaissance sectorielle : Une maîtrise approfondie de l’industrie de la construction au Québec, du marché de la main-d’œuvre et des réglementations de la Commission de la construction du Québec (CCQ). 
 Aptitudes linguistiques : La maîtrise du français à l’oral et à l’écrit (l’anglais constitue un atout apprécié). 
 Préféré : 
 Leadership d'influence : Une aisance marquée à évoluer au sein d'une organisation matricielle et à rallier des équipes multidisciplinaires par la force de la persuasion. 
 Mobilité : La flexibilité nécessaire pour effectuer des déplacements réguliers sur les différents sites de travail au Québec (jusqu'à 30 % du temps).

The Architectural Site Superintendent leads the safe, coordinated and productive field execution of assigned architectural trade packages across Ontario Line South station work areas. The role supervises subcontractors and self-perform resources, confirms work-front readiness, coordinates interfaces with civil, structural, mechanical, electrical and systems teams, and drives work to approved drawings, specifications, quality requirements and project milestones.
 This is a hands-on field leadership role. The successful candidate will establish clear daily priorities, remove constraints before they affect production, maintain reliable site records, and lead architectural fit-out from area release through inspection, deficiency close-out and turnover.
 Key Accountabilities: 
 Field Leadership, Sueprvision & Productivity 
 Lead daily field operations for assigned architectural work areas and communicate priorities, sequence, constraints and changes to forepersons, subcontractors and field coordinators.
 Coordinate labour, supervision, equipment, access and materials across architectural packages such as façade, roofing, partitions, wall cladding, ceilings, flooring, doors and hardware, millwork, metalwork, painting, signage and architectural specialties, as applicable.
 Chair daily pre-start and coordination huddles; confirm crews understand the work plan, approved information, interfaces and expected production.
 Monitor installation progress and workforce utilization, address field conflicts promptly, and escalate material risks with recommended actions.
 Support a respectful, inclusive and accountable site culture across a diverse workforce.
 Health, Safety, Environment & Emergency Readiness 
 Demonstrate visible safety leadership and enforce the project HSE plan, permits, procedures and site rules.
 Confirm hazard assessments, safe work plans, toolbox talks, inspections and corrective actions are complete and suitable before and during work.
 Stop unsafe work, correct hazards, report incidents and near misses, and participate in investigations and preventive actions.
 Coordinate safe access, housekeeping, temporary protection, lifting and hoisting, work at height, hot work, silica and dust controls, confined spaces and other high-risk activities, where applicable.
 Work with HSE and logistics teams to ensure emergency arrangements, exclusion zones and public or third-party interfaces are maintained.
 Planning, Schedule, Logistics & Trade Interfaces 
 Develop and maintain detailed short-term plans and three- to six-week look-ahead schedules aligned with contractual milestones and area handover dates.
 Coordinate architectural works with civil, structural, waterproofing, firestopping, MEP, vertical transportation, communications, security, signage, testing and commissioning interfaces.
 Track quantities and actual progress against plan; identify variance, critical constraints and out-of-sequence work; implement recovery or resequencing measures with the project team.
 Coordinate deliveries, laydown, hoisting, material storage, environmental conditions and protection of finished work in constrained station areas.
 Quality, Technical Control, Records & Cost Awareness 
 Ensure installations comply with approved drawings, specifications, samples and mock-ups, manufacturers requirements, method statements, inspection and test plans, and project quality procedures.
 Coordinate first-work inspections, hold points, testing, field reviews, deficiencies, non-conformances and turnover records with Quality, Design and Engineering teams.
 Verify architectural tolerances, substrates, openings, elevations, setting-out and interface conditions before installation; prevent concealment of incomplete or unaccepted work.
 Maintain complete daily reports covering labour, equipment, installed quantities, deliveries, weather and environmental conditions, delays, safety, quality, access restrictions and changed conditions.
 Preserve records supporting progress measurement, as-built information, change management, subcontract administration and claims avoidance; identify potential cost and schedule impacts early.

 Demonstrated delivery of architectural fit-out or finish scopes on complex transit, infrastructure, commercial, institutional or high-rise projects.
 Experience coordinating multiple trades in constrained, high-activity areas and taking work through inspection, deficiency close-out and turnover.
 Strong understanding of architectural drawings, specifications, shop drawings, reflected ceiling plans, room data, finish schedules, details, tolerances, sequencing and subcontract scope boundaries.
 Proven field leadership, planning, coordination, conflict-resolution and decision-making skills.
 Ability to identify incomplete design information and constructability or interface risks, initiate RFIs, and communicate practical field solutions without bypassing approval processes.
 Ability to interpret schedule information, measure progress, identify constraints and develop practical recovery plans.
 Clear written and verbal communication, including concise daily reporting and timely escalation of safety, quality, schedule and commercial risk.
 Commercial awareness regarding labour, material, equipment, productivity, delays, rework and changed conditions.

 Ontario supervisor health and safety awareness training.
 Working at Heights, WHMIS and project-specific training as required for assigned duties.

About the company 
 Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. This is a task-based, independent contractor opportunity, not an employment relationship. Participation is limited to this project.
 Project Highlights 
 Earnings per approved task: a fixed rate for each task, set in advance
 Fully self-scheduled: no minimum hours and no set schedule; you choose which tasks to take and when
 Remote: open to US-licensed physicians based in eligible US states
 No patient contact, no malpractice exposure: you review written clinical cases
 All contributors are license-verified physicians
 $50 one-time onboarding reward, paid once your first task on the project is approved
 What this project involves 
 We're looking for physicians (MD/DO) with an active, unrestricted US medical license to evaluate clinical EHR vignettes for a medical AI evaluation project. General and internal medicine are the main focus. Each task is a written clinical case, assessed against the project's acceptance criteria. Contributors may:
 Evaluate clinical EHR vignettes paired with a question, a proposed answer, and a distractor "trap" answer across diagnosis and treatment tasks, spanning cardiovascular, nervous, hematologic, respiratory, digestive, urinary, reproductive, musculoskeletal, and integumentary systems;
 Score the clinical reasoning quality of benchmark items: vignette accuracy and completeness, whether the vignette gives the answer away, answer correctness and gradeability, and trap quality;
 Check whether the reasoning chain reaches the answer from vignette facts alone, correct reasoning traces, and write short rationales.
 Each case receives three independent blind reads, followed by physician adjudication. Real clinical complexity only. You're improving the AI tools you'll eventually use yourself.
 What we look for 
 This project is a good fit for US-licensed physicians looking for a flexible, time-limited project they can fit around their other commitments. Ideally, contributors will have:
 Medical degree (MD or DO) and an active, unrestricted US medical license (verified at onboarding and re-checked monthly);
 Board certification or completed residency training, with direct patient care experience (attending-level preferred). Practising or retired physicians welcome;
 Broad, multi-system diagnostic and treatment experience (internal, family, emergency, or hospital medicine);
 Strong clinical reasoning: differential diagnosis, next-step management, and application of evidence-based guidelines;
 Prior experience in medical AI evaluation, clinical content or exam-question review, or medical annotation/QA (a plus);
 Strong written English (C1+).
 This project is not suitable for medical students, unlicensed medical graduates, non-physician clinicians (NPs, PAs, nurses, pharmacists), or non-clinical healthcare titles.
 How it works 
 Apply → Pass qualification(s) → Join the project → Complete tasks → Get paid for approved tasks
 Flexibility 
 You decide whether, when, and how much to contribute. There are no minimum hours, set schedules, or required availability. Task availability varies with project phases. Tasks are submitted through the platform and are approved when they meet the project’s acceptance criteria.
 Earnings 
 Earnings are paid only for completed and approved tasks. Each task type has a fixed rate. There is no time tracking and no hour logging. There are no tiers or speed adjustments to the rate. QA and adjudication tasks have a higher per-task rate.
 $50 one-time onboarding reward, paid once your first task on the project is approved.
 Quality incentives: additional earnings for high-quality approved tasks, on terms set out in the project guidelines.
